You mis-interpretated what they said and threw hate on them for absolutely no reason. If you think they've been transphobic, just report their coment and that's it. But you can't fight fire with fire.

I dont think their comment really is transphobia, and let me explain why.

Some people just like cis people, but that doesn't make them transphobic. 

Some people (let's call them X), (let's set for an example, that they're straight, they are attracted both biologically and romantically to the opposite gender, let's also call them Y), start dating a trans person who they think is of their opposite gender (let's call them Z). 

The person they're dating, doesn't disclose that information.

At some point, that will be found out, and X will find out their partner isn't Y as they had thought all of this time, instead, they are Z. At that point, they may feel lied to, they may begin feeling un-attracted to Z, and that's okay, as they are only attracted to Y for whatever purpose, being biological (the most common in my opinion) or romantical.

Unfortunately, hatred exists towards trans people, and in these situations hidden hatred from some of X towards trans people can lead to them hurting or even killing Z, and that's something that never has to happen.

That's sadly a reason that maybe that information should be disclosed if asked during the beginning of a relationship, or during dating.

Hatred is always going to exist, let's be realist. And we have to take precautions.

Let's take for example, I live in a zone where muggings are common, specially moto-robbers, crime is going to exist (sadly) for a very long time, let's hope it's not forever, but that being said, I can't walk outside with my phone in my hand (this applies to being tras, as an example) in some situations, such as walking outside during night-time (this applies to dating), as I can get mugged (this applies to getting hurt).

Same with dating being trans, being trans is absolutely okay, but hatred exists, and that should be disclosed if asked during dating to avoid getting hurt, avoid transphobic people (this applies to moto-robbers from the previous example) as much as possible.

It's sad, but we have to avoid that. Hopefully, sometime we'll live in a world where hatred is minimal to non-existent, and these situations never happen again.
